title: A cluster inside a 4-vCPU quota
scenario: "We have exactly 4 vCPUs in the region. Bring up the cluster, and tell me whether a Kubernetes upgrade would even fit." — Engineering manager
mission: Apply 40-aks, measure quota usage and record the capacity decision (nodes, autoscaler and upgrade surge) as an ADR.
objectives: Write a decision record with trade-offs
cost: ≈ US$3/day while running (2 × D2s_v5). Stop it at night: az aks stop.

steps.title: Check quota first
steps.detail: Total Regional vCPUs and DSv5 family.
steps.command: az vm list-usage --location eastus2 -o table | Select-String "Total Regional vCPUs|DSv5"

steps.title: Apply
steps.detail: Start it and do something else.

steps.title: Do the math
steps.detail: Autoscaler max 2 nodes × 2 vCPU + max_surge 33% during an upgrade: does it fit in 4?

criteria.text: Regional vCPU usage is within the quota
ADR-0008 exists with Context, Decision and Consequences sections and the quota numbers

expectedResult: A running cluster and a written answer to "can we upgrade?"
recovery: QuotaExceeded on apply: reduce max_count or VM size via variables, never by hand.
dont: Do not request a quota increase before reasoning about the alternatives
Do not leave the cluster running overnight
hints: Surge nodes are extra nodes created during an upgrade.
33% of 2 nodes rounds up to 1 extra node.
Options: scale to 1 node before upgrading, a smaller surge, or a temporary quota increase.

interview.question: Your cluster upgrade fails with a quota error. Walk me through the diagnosis and the options.

debrief: At 2 nodes, max_surge 33% adds 1 node (6 vCPU > 4): the upgrade fails. Choices: upgrade at 1 node, reduce surge (slower, riskier), or temporary quota. The ADR makes the trade-off explicit for the next engineer.

checker.plan: Read-only: az aks show, az vm list-usage; offline: ADR-0008 headings.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs a deployed cluster.
